The language used for the development was JAVA 8 and the database management system was PostgreSQL. The results obtained through graphics and reports allow to the designer to view different designs and results for a chosen set of technologies and components combinations for the assembly of a static converter prototype. Hence, making the design task less complex and quick according to the restrictions and input data set by the designer.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control applied on a three-level single-phase T-converter rectifier
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work proposes the modelling and simulation of a single-phase AC/DC half-bridge T-type converter by using a Sliding Mode Control algorithm, which is little sensitive to disturbances and displays fast dynamic behavior. The control ensures unity power factor, sinusoidal input currents, regulated DC output voltage, and a three level converter grid voltage. This paper also compares the proposed solution with a conventional control algorithm with PWM.

articleTitle: An isolated three-phase power-factor correction rectifier using an autotransformer and two single-phase single-stage rectifiers
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents an isolated three-phase power-factor correction rectifier using a Scott autotransformer and using two single-phase single-stage (S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) isolated current rectifiers with power factor correction, based on a Full-Bridge Flyback converter. The Scott autotransformer provides a phase reduction allowing the use of two single-phase rectifiers. The proposed converter can operate as a step-down or a step-up voltage, according to the input and output voltage levels. This paper presents the theoretical analysis of the converter for continuous conduction mode (CCM) as well as experimental results based on a 4 kW prototype.

articleTitle: A new half-bridge Hybrid Switched-Capacitor inverter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: In this paper, a new inverter topology is proposed. The new topology is based on the Hybrid Switched Capacitor (HSC) cell, which brings the advantages of Switched Capacitor Converters (SCC) combined with the conventional ones. In addition to that, it presents a conversion ratio equal to half of the conventional inverter, and each power switch blocks a half of the dc bus voltage. Also, the voltage across the capacitors are balanced and limited to half of the input voltage. The proposed inverter is suitable for practical applications where the peak value of the ac load voltage is lower than the half of the input voltage.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a prototype of a single phase converter for photovoltaic systems connected to the grid
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: The usage of electrical energy generation with alternative sources is increasing significantly, due to the general concern about the environment and generation with nonrenewable sources. This fact encourages the development of technologies and new researches, to come up with solutions to allow the connection the new systems to the grid in a safe and trustable way. This work presents the project and construction of a prototype of 1,44[kW] monophasic converter for photovoltaic panels, considering the operation in connection with the grid (127[V], 60[Hz]). For the synchronism between the photovoltaic system and the AC grid a PLL (phase-locked loop) was implemented, carrying out the angle detection in the grid. Experimental and simulated results are presented to confirm the operation of the designed and implemented prototype.

articleTitle: Simplified modeling and control of a high-power high-voltage isolated dc-dc converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents the modelling and control strategy for a new high-power multilevel multipulse medium frequency-isolated dc-dc converter. The new converter is composed by a Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) associated to an isolated Multipulse Rectifier (MR). Its application is targeted to non-conventional distribution and sub-transmission systems, while operating at tens of kVs and a few MWs. Experimental results of a digital controlled downsized prototype are also presented.

articleTitle: Voltage and current control of self-excited Switched Reluctance Generator for variable speed drive
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper deals with the Switched Reluctance Generator (SRG), working in self excitation mode, for controlled generated voltage operation in variable speed environment. The inherent behavior observed is the existence of high amounts of reactive power circulating between the machine windings and the excitation capacitors that lead to high peaks of phase currents. These high currents, due to wide excursions in magnetic flux, can impose restrictions in the applications of the machine. It is observed that this high amount of reactive power is not necessary to reach given specifications in generated voltages. Therefore, the paper investigates a way to overcome this problem, through the control of the machine's phase currents. It is shown that with controlled phase currents the generator still delivers desired voltages and power, within a range of speed variation. The work explores the current control strategy based on controlling the phase switching angles, through hysteresis control. Block diagram of the control system is presented, along with the state space model of the SRG, which includes the saturation of the magnetic circuit. The complete set is simulated and the results are presented and discussed. Bench experiments are carried out to validate the simulation findings, where all control circuitry is developed in digital environment using the TMS320F28335 DSP platform. These experimental results are also included.

articleTitle: Three-phase/four-wire dc/ac converters based on three- and two-level legs
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: In this paper, four three-phase/four-wire dc/ac converter topologies assembled with three-level and two-level legs are proposed. Several relevant characteristics of the converters are addressed, such as voltage capability, harmonic distortion, and power losses. Experimental and simulated results are presented.

articleTitle: Low-cost platform for electrical measurement and frequency analysis in power electronic education
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: In recent years, power electronics utilization in modern devices has experienced a large growth due to several applications. For this reason, undergraduate laboratory courses in this field should have modern equipment for measurement and analysis of electrical signals. With this, students will have the opportunity to understand theoretical concepts in practice. However, commercial equipment of this nature have high finance costs. This is an obstacle for undergraduate courses with financial restrictions. This paper presents the development and testing of a low-cost platform for electrical measurement and frequency spectrum analysis, conceived to improve power electronics education. Experimental results done with different types of loads, such as power electronics converters, demonstrated acceptable measurements when compared with commercial equipment.

articleTitle: A dimmable charge-pump ZVS led driver with PFC
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents a dimmable charge-pump driver to power light-emitting diodes (LEDs) with power factor correction (PFC) and Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS). The proposed LED driver does not utilize electrolytic capacitors, providing a high useful lifetime, and it can stabilize the output current in open loop control without needing current sensors, which reduces the cost. The output power is proportional to the switching frequency, which allows the LEDs dimming. A prototype with 22 W was implemented and experimental results were discussed. The prototype presented a power factor of 0.996 and an efficiency of 89.5 %. The driver output power was reduced by more than 40% through the switching frequency while varying of 53 kHz to 30 kHz and the converter has continues to operate in ZVS.

articleTitle: Transformerless interleaving multilevel NPC inverter for photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a transformerless multilevel NPC (Neutral Point Clamped) inverter for grid-connected photovoltaic systems, applying the concept of high power density, using Gallium Nitride power transistors and employing interleaving strategy for reducing the weight/volume of the passive filter elements. It also presented an equivalent circuit, it is possible to study the issue of ripple in output current, circulating current and inductor current. Are shown results of theoretical analysis as well as simulation results for power 1kW.

articleTitle: Low rating hybrid power filter for application in distribution systems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of the application of a hybrid filter (HF) in low voltage distribution systems with linear and nonlinear loads. In the proposed topology, the passive filter (PF) is tuned at third and fifth harmonics, even in situations in which the active filter (AF) is disconnected, and the AF has low rating due his distinct connection to the system. The flexibility and viability of this topology will be proved through mathematical analysis and simulations.

articleTitle: Design of z-source converter dc/dc for a photovoltaic system connected to dc microgrid
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper proposes the research and implementation of DC/DC ZSC operating in CCM, applied on photovoltaic system for DC microgrid. The DC microgrid consists of PV panel, wind turbine, battery, DC loads and a grid-connected inverter system. To ensure the stability of a DC microgrid, the power flow within the DC microgrid must be balanced at all times to maintain a constant DC bus voltage. For such aim, PV array are connected to DC/DC ZSC input and it provides high gain voltage from 221 Vdc to 400Vdc in its output connected to DC microgrid bus. As the power supplied by PV Panel depends on the load and the climatic conditions (insolation and temperature), extracting maximum power and converter are required. So, two different types of MPPT techniques controls are proposed Perturb and observe (P&O) and Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC). This paper focuses mostly on P&O and through PSIM simulations are presented the behavior of system attending that output power is 1.38 kW.

articleTitle: Sorting algorithm for a pd modulation for a cascaded multilevel converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple phase disposition modulation with sorting algorithm for three-phase cascaded multilevel converters. The sorting algorithm can be implemented entirely in software. The main features of the proposed modulation is a better distribution of PWM pulses, switching losses and DC bus current when compared with the conventional phase disposition (PD) modulation. In addition, it results in the nearest level PWM in the line-to-line output voltages leading to a smaller THD if compared with phase-shifted (PS) modulation. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the good performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Next generation arc welding machines based on Silicon Carbide MOSFETS and high frequency planar magnetics
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: Silicon Carbide (SiC) Power MOSFET devices are rapidly being introduced in different applications due their advantages over their silicon (Si) counterparts. Higher switching frequency (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sw</sub>) coupled with planar magnetics opens new possibilities in terms of increasing the power density of converter, while also improving their efficiency and lowering costs. In this paper, SiC MOSFETS and planar magnetics are employed to demonstrate new possibilities in arc welding machines technology. Design details of high power density power source for a multi-process welding machine are presented. Test results for 3.9kW/150A and 200 kHz switching frequency working at rated load and under over load condition are included.

articleTitle: Comparative performance evaluation of magnetic couplers for Wireless Power Transfer applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: A magnetic coupler is a system composed by an emitter inductor and a receiver inductor existing between them a certain magnetic coupling. The geometric shape of these inductors determine the performance of the coupler under lateral, axial or angular misalignment, affecting the power transferred to the load in a Wireless Power Transfer application. The objective of this paper is to compare couplers in terms of uncompensated apparent power, self inductance variation and coupling coefficient variation under spatial misalignment between emitter and receiver, based on a hypothetical application example. Finite element method simulations are used. Also, the simulations are employed to identify geometric parameters strongly correlated with uncompensated power.

articleTitle: Dc current balancing control of a three-phase five-level bidirectional buck+boost-type converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work proposes a dc current balancing control for a three-phase high-power factor five-level buck+boost-type converter. The converter act as both a rectifier or as an inverter interfacing residential dc power distribution systems to the ac grid. A pulse width modulation with two symmetrically phase-shifted carriers drives the converter in an interleaved operation with interphase transformers (IPT's). The modulation pattern ideally leads to null average voltages across the IPT's at each switching period, but if an imbalance occurs the IPT's saturation must be avoided. Novel feedback control scheme and modulation strategy that allows dc current balancing are described in this work. The effectiveness of the dc current balancing is verified in an experimental prototype.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a high efficiency AC-AC Buck converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents an AC-AC Buck converter in which a modulation technique was applied in order to reduce losses due to dissipative snubbers. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulation were performed. A 100W prototype was built and tested. Efficiency curves show that snubber losses are minimized with the use of a simple open-loop control technique.

articleTitle: Selective harmonic currents suppressing applied to a three-phase shunt active power filter based on adaptive filters
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a selective strategy used to generate the harmonic current references, which are employed in the control loops of a three-phase active power filter (APF). By applying the aforementioned selective strategy, the selection of the harmonic components that will be suppressed by means of the filter is allowed. The proposed strategy comprises of an algorithm based on the synchronous reference frame. In addition, it uses adaptive filters in order to carry out the harmonic components selection. The APF topology is implemented by using a four-leg inverter, which is mathematically modelled in two-phase stationary reference frame (αβ0-axes). Due to the inherent decoupling in the αβ0-axes, proportional and integrative controllers are used in each one of the referred coordinates, allowing the individual control of the compensation currents. The SRF-based algorithm is mathematically analyzed, as well as experimental results are presented in order to validate the theoretical development.

articleTitle: A five-phase PWM rectifier: Analysis, modeling, control and simulation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed analysis of two-level bidirectional five-phase PWM rectifier. The operation of the rectifier in steady-state is described, including the modulation strategy. Modeling of the rectifier is developed in rotational reference frame and small-signal models for phase current and output voltage control are presented. A control strategy in dq frame is presented to ensure the operation with unity power factor. Finally, simulation results are presented to verify the operation of the five-phase rectifier in steady-state and dynamic conditions, also operation with reverse power flow is presented.

articleTitle: Center-point-clamped ac-ac direct power converter with considerations for input side filter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: A novel topology for direct ac-ac power conversion has been introduced recently. This topology employs a clamping structure so as to reduce the voltage stress on the switching power semiconductor devices. This paper analyzes the dynamics of this center-point-clamped converter by taking the input filter components into consideration. Simulation results presented in the paper verify the efficacy of the designed input and output filter in attenuating the current harmonics in the input side and the voltage harmonics in the output side. A small scale laboratory prototype has been built to prove the practical realization. Experimental waveforms obtained also confirm the already obtained analytical and simulation results.

articleTitle: Three-phase high power factor single-stage AC/DC DCM SEPIC converter with bidirectional switches
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a three-phase high power factor AC/DC converter based on SEPIC converter with bidirectional switches. The converter operates in DCM as a voltage follower where the input currents waveforms follow the voltages waveforms without current control loops. This single-stage converter has high reliability, since it employs four active switches and six high frequency diodes for AC/DC conversion with high power factor and high frequency isolation. Regarding the control system, it is composed by a single DC output voltage control loop (such as an output voltage control of a DC-DC converter). The four active switches are command with the same gate signal. Therefore, the PWM modulator is realized with a sawtooth waveform, performing a trailing edge modulation. Simulation results and the assembly of the prototype from a converter with 127 V input voltage, 200 V output voltage, 50 kHz switching frequency and 3000 W output power are also presented.

articleTitle: A single-phase isolated AC-DC converter using an interleaved MMC
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work introduces a single-phase isolated ac-dc topology using an interleaved modular multilevel converter. There is a medium frequency transformer which provides the galvanic isolation and operates at 10 kHz, allowing the weight and volume reduction. Also, the transformer connects a modular multilevel converter with coupled interphase inductors at the high voltage side to a full-bridge converter at the low voltage side. The modular multilevel converter provides the current and voltage distribution in the submodules reducing the efforts on the switches while the full-bridge phase-shift converter controls the bidirectional power flow. The topology is well suitable for a wide range of medium voltage applications such as solid-state transformers, ac or dc distributed power systems and renewable energy systems. The principle of operation and the control scheme are presented. The topology validation is made through simulation concerning a single-phase converter with 13.8 kV / 60 Hz input line voltage, 4 submodules with 10 kHz switching frequency per arm, 11.27 kV/800 V - 10 kHz medium frequency transformer, 800 V dc output voltage and 100 kW power rating.

articleTitle: A new class of Switched-Linear Converters
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This article presents a new class of hybrid converters named Switched-Linear (SL) Converters that can operate as a DC-DC, DC-AC or AC-DC converter. The idea is originated from conventional linear power amplifier integrated with a switched power converter. The linear power unit/cell is a power amplifier, which is fed by two tracking power supplies to boost the efficiency of the linear unit without scarifying any virtues of linear power amplifier. It can be achieved making the voltage in the linear amplifier the lowest possible level and adequate to application. The main goal is to guarantee the possibility of drain reversal power energy whenever it processes reversal power flux and/or non-resistive loads. Therefore, by combining the linear power amplifier with the switched power amplifier, the system has synthetic performance of high fidelity, high efficiency and excellent dynamic characteristics.

articleTitle: A new topology for fuel cell power trains including a new integrated converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: A new power train topology for fuel cell based vehicles with electrical machines is introduced, including a new combined converter. A new direct energy conversion scheme is applied, reducing the contributing components to the standard power train setup while increasing efficiency due to direct energy conversion. Using this power train configuration, a standard inverter is used in parallel for energy conversion in terms of propulsion demands and charging aspects. For the first time power arising from a fuel cell stack and accumulator are converted at the same time with one standard power train inverter offering high efficiency and increased reliability.

articleTitle: Strategy control converter to enhance the performance in the grid-connected PMSG wind power generation system
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: Currently, there are several power converter topologies applied to wind power generation. The converters allow the use of wind turbines operating at variable speed, enabling better use of wind forces. The high performance of the converters is being increasingly demanded, mainly because of the increase in the power generation capacity by wind turbines, which gave rise to various converter topologies, such as parallel or multilevel converters. The use of converters allow effective control of the power injected into the grid, either partially, for the case using partial converter, or total control for the case of using full converter. In this work, is proposed an implementation of a wind cogeneration system using a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) associated with a power converter, in order to inject active power and improve harmonics compensation in the electrical power grid, in according to standard IEEE and IEC. The control strategy of the active power delivered to the grid by cogeneration is based on the philosophy of indirect control.

articleTitle: SVFT-based current control applied to a three-phase active power filter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents the application of the recently published control based on the Space-Vector Fourier Transform (SVFT) to the current compensation of a conventional three-phase active power filter. This current control achieves a fast and precise tracking of specific positive- or negative-sequence harmonic components, characteristics inherited by the space-vector Fourier transform, which is a discrete Fourier transform suitable for detecting harmonic sequences of three-phase signals. Moreover, other advantages of the applied current control are: it is naturally a discrete-time control, avoiding problems related to discretization methods; it is possible to compensate multiple harmonics and sequences using only one controller; its recursive implementation presents low computational burden. Due to these characteristics, the SVFT-based control can be applied in an active power filter for compensating harmonic and unbalance current components typical of non-linear loads. In order to show the feasibility of the control strategy, simulations are performed and experimental results are obtained on a prototype.

articleTitle: Linear temperature model for fuel cell simulators
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: Alternative sources of energy has been the subject of study by researchers, is the need to master the technology or by the growing demand for renewable energy sources. Many studies have turned to survey models for simulation of fuel cells as an aid in the manufacture of electronic circuits for integration and use of energy generated by this kind of power source, due to the high cost of these equipments and used fuel (hydrogen). This work hereby presents a simulation model that includes the effect of the variation of temperature with the requested cell current. Such a model has been developed from tests on a fuel cell of 1,2kW - Nexa Power Module, using the identification by the method of least squares with pseudo-random binary signals and optimization tools.

articleTitle: Voltage and frequency regulation of induction generator based system applying proportional-resonant controller
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper deals with a system control for voltage and frequency regulation in stand-alone generation systems based on self-excited induction generators (SEIG). A three-wire hybrid topology composed by switchable capacitor banks and distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) is considered. The DSTATCOM is controlled by proportional-resonant-derivative (PRD) controllers in association to proportional-integral (PI) controllers in order to compensate the system reactive power, balance induction generator (IG) currents and compensate harmonic currents. An electronic load controller connected to the three-phase bus guarantee the frequency regulation by the control of active power. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate its performance.

articleTitle: Robust stability analysis based on quadratic Lyapunov functions applied to power electronics
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper investigates the stability based on Lyapunov functions with application to power converters affected by slowly or arbitrarily fast time-varying parameters. The limitations of the stability based on exhaustive pole evaluations, a commonly used approach in power electronics, are discussed, and the advantages of the stability analysis by means of Lyapunov functions are shown.

articleTitle: A solar-powered VRLA battery charge controller using a dc-dc Ćuk converter for a telemetry station power supply
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work presents the development of a charge controller which uses the energy of a photovoltaic panel to charge a valve regulated lead-acid (VRLA) battery for an autonomous telemetry station energy system. A Ćuk converter is employed to adequate the power generated from the panel to the battery. A three-stage charge control strategy based on the I-U technique is applied in order to charge the battery quickly and preserve its lifetime. A maximum power point tracking technique based on temperature measurement is used to provide a quick charge to the battery.

articleTitle: A novel modular multilevel inverter for medium-voltage open-end split winding machines based on single-phase submodules with input-series connection
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: In this paper, a modular inverter topology conceived by input series connection of H-bridge (ISHB) is presented and verified trough experimental results. The proposed converter is naturally appropriate for open-end split winding induction motor drive due to the galvanic isolation offered by the machine. Each sub-module is composed by a H-bridge inverter, which is characterized for a modulation with three levels, using phase-shifted PWM modulation strategy. All bus capacitor related to a phase of inverter are connected in series to reach the desired voltage level that is required in high power and high input voltage applications requirements. The proposed structure has a voltage self-balance in the series-connected input capacitors, which provides a stable operating point and ensures proper power distribution between each submodule. A prototype was build in order to validate the theoretical results for a 7.50kW induction motor, that has three-open winding per phase.

articleTitle: Comparison of sensorless techniques based on Model Reference Adaptive System for induction motor drives
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of sensorless vector control strategies for Induction Motor (IM). The strategies includes an Indirect Field Orientation Control (IFOC) and a Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS). Several studies have been proposed in the literature concerning different approaches of MRAS estimators. In this work, an evaluation is performed of three MRAS approaches for estimate the rotor speed from different models: rotor flux, back electromotive force (back-EMF) and instantaneous reactive power. Matlab simulations are performed to test the proposed strategy for different speed and sensitivity of such drives to parameters variations. To verify the approach to sensorless techniques with variations of speed in real conditions a drive for the prototype was assembled and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Madeira river complex HVDC system: A dynamic behavior study using PSCAD
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work aims to present the dynamical study regarding the HVDC link of Madeira river hydroelectric complex, which is composed by Santo Antônio and Jirau hydropower plants located in southeastern Brazil, whose total installed capacity is 6,900 MW. The HVDC system comprises two 3,150-MW bipolar links and two back-to-back stations rated at 400 MW. The analysis is based on simulations of the system model using PSCAD/EMTDC software. The obtained results are also compared with actual system data provided by ONS through a RAP for validation purposes.

articleTitle: Modeling and control of a high power current source for sirius - the new Brazilian Synchrotron Light Source
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work presents the mathematical model of a high power and precision current source to supply electromagnets that will be used in the new Brazilian Synchrotron Light Source. Moreover, three control techniques that minimize the interference of input voltage variations on the output current are analyzed: PI controller with single loop, PI controller with double loop and PI controller associated with feedforward controller. The validity and analysis of the study are performed by comparing the simulations with experimental tests. The feedforward control has showed the best results, presenting negligible deviation from the reference current.

articleTitle: A novel 5-level hybrid rectifier using bypass concept for electric vehicle onboard battery charging
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel 5-level three-phase PFC rectifier, appropriate for electric vehicle (EV) onboard battery charging systems, using an approach known as bypass concept. In contrast to the standard approach, where two power stages always work in series (PFC + step-down), such serial operation takes place here only during a brief interval of time. The characteristics of the proposed system, including the principle of operation, modulation strategy, dimensioning equations and calculated losses, are described in detail. Finally, the feasibility of the 5-level hybrid rectifier with bypass function is demonstrated by means of a 22 kW hardware prototype.

articleTitle: Fractional order controller PIλ designed via heuristic optimization algorithm Lévy-Flight Firefly for connection of renewable energy sources to the grid
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: The connection of renewable energy sources to the grid, in a way that characterizes distributed generation, enables the optimization of local available natural resources. These sources should be managed in order to produce a distortion-free AC terminal voltage, and to inject in the grid the power that is not consumed by the local load. In the system here analyzed for connection of renewable energy sources to the grid, the AC terminal voltage is controlled via a proportional resonant controller. For most loads this solution is satisfactory, however, for a parallel RLC load with the resonant frequency equal the fundamental frequency of the grid, the system has characteristics of instability with an unacceptable amount of harmonic distortion at the Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) terminals. Due to the limited bandwidth of classical PI controller, and the undesired behavior of the proportional resonant controller for RLC load, this paper proposes the use of a fractional order PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup> controller instead of a proportional resonant controller at the fundamental frequency. For design of the fractional order controller we employed a heuristic optimization algorithm to obtain a stable response with attenuation around 0 dB at the fundamental frequency and total harmonic distortion smaller than 5%.

articleTitle: Resonant filtering technique to detect symmetric components under unbalanced conditions for control of Active Front End converters
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents a discrete implementation of a complex resonant structure using a mathematical transformation for detection of symmetrical components, for the control of Neutral Point Clamped Three Level Active Front End. The symmetrical positive-negative sequences components of the grid voltage need to be separated to properly orient the control the converter. This prevents oscillations at twice the fundamental frequency on the reference currents on the synchronous reference frame, allowing for current tracking with zero steady state error.

articleTitle: Circulating current mitigation in Dual Active Bridge converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work brings forward a new methodology to maximize the efficiency of Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter for its several patterns of operation. This goal is reached by the mitigation of its processed circulating energy. It is proposed a figure of merit which relates the average input current and the RMS current of the power transfer inductor, and an algorithm to select the trio of control variables (D1, D2, φ) ensuring that this objective is achieved. It has been performed a detailed steady-state analysis of every pattern for all the possible modulations, as well as the identification of all commutations under zero voltage of the Full-Bridges that compose the DAB. Due to the twelve different modulation patterns presented by the DAB that affect directly the operation mode, the design, the volume, the weight, and different performances can be achieved. In this way, it is verified the impact of the control variables on converter efficiency, as well its relationships with the average input current and the RMS inductor current. Results show that the converter efficiency obtained for different operation points making the use of the developed algorithm are very close to those obtained making the computation by the optimal converter efficiency.

articleTitle: A controlled dynamic braking of a separate excitation DC machine
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper aims at demonstrating that a separate excitation for a DC machine can have its dynamic braking optimized via a significant reduction of its elapsed time.

articleTitle: Dynamic analysis of a ZVS bidirectional isolated three-phase dc-dc converter using phase-shift control
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents the dynamic analysis, simulation and experimental results on a ZVS (zero voltage switching) bidirectional isolated three-phase dc-dc converter. The topology uses a steady-state model based on fundamental components considering three possible control variables (dual phase-shift and duty cycle). The dynamic model of the converter using phase-shift (PS) control is developed employing the gyrator theory. Simulation results are presented to validate the plant model and test the digital control system. Implementation is performed in an FPGA (field-programmable gate array) device and closed-loop experimental results are discussed.

articleTitle: Enhancing photovoltaic applications with embedded circuitry within the solar panels
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work presents the enhanced functionalities of a solar panel when embedded circuitry is included in its construction. A voltage sweep allows to track the global maximum power point even in presence of partial shading, which is transmitted to a DC/DC converter in order to maximize the transferred power. This voltage sweep also allows to determine the operating condition of the photovoltaic module, thanks to a suitable algorithm, which is capable to generate an alarm signal when abnormal conditions are detected in the voltage-power curve. The inclusion of a central server allows to statistically process the information in order to prevent or predict evitable failures.

articleTitle: 225A/22V high precision current source using interleaved modules and Digital Regulation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents a first prototype of a high power high stable current source with digital control that will be used in the new Brazilian Synchrotron Source. The output rate is 225A/22V and its topology is based on two Buck converters operating in parallel and in the interleaving mode. This work presents the conceptual design and the first results, as well the detected problems.

articleTitle: Proposal of a power flow control strategy applied to a hybrid microgrid
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper proposes an energy management system designed to control the power flow in a hybrid microgrid composed of a 1 kWp PV array, a 1.2 kWp wind turbine, a 1.2 kW fuel cell and a 31.5 F / 250 V supercapacitor bank. The microgrid provides uninterrupted power supply of critical dc loads and it can operate in both, standalone or grid-connected modes. A power flow control strategy is proposed to provide real time power references for each renewable energy source according to the operational mode (grid-connected or standalone), the availability of energy resources (solar, wind and hydrogen stock) and the priority of dispatch. Experimental results obtained from several arrangements of power generation and load demand are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Simplified energy-efficient current control of the PMSG based WECS machine side converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work aims to model the machine side of a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based wind energy conversion system (WECS), which makes use of full scale power electronic converter (PEC). In order to verify the behavior of the wind turbine control system, the current control of the machine side converter (MSC) is implemented in two different circuits: one with a classical three-phase three-level bidirectional inverter and the other arising from the substitution of each arm of the inverter by a controlled voltage source. Thus, the circuitry is simplified and the simulation time is reduced, without affecting the controllers, and is therefore a simplification option to be implemented in larger models, such as wind farms connected to the electric power system, besides being useful for the design of other current controllers and current signals filters.

articleTitle: Steady state analysis of separated DC-link universal power line conditioner
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents important characteristics on the study of universal filters topologies. The integration of series and shunt active power filter was proposed in the work of Fujita and Akagi (1998), where the two converter shared the same dc-link bus voltage. By a steady state analysis it was noted that there is a significant difference between two voltage converters. The voltage capability of shunt convert is bigger than series converter for the most cases. This way, the authors analysis a topology with two dc-link voltages, to better design the converters voltages capabilities, consequently reduce the THD and power loss. By the steady state analysis it possible to show the limits of operation and the better parameters for: transformer turn ration and passive filters.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of two islanding detection methods in multi-inverter case
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper compares the effectiveness of two active islanding detection methods in multi-inverter configuration. The methods are based on frequency and voltage positive feedback. The Run-On Time (islanded operation time) is investigated in a typical residential distribution network arrangement, with different ratios of inverter power to load power. Performance degradation is observed in simultaneous operation of these methods, depending on how much power is injected by each inverter to electrical system. Simulations and the adopted models are supported by experimental results.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic system with bumpless transfer between grid-connected and stand-alone modes
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper discuses a Quasi-Uninterrupted Power Supply (Q-UPS) with photovoltaic (PV) grid-connected system to increase energy production for local consumption. The purpose of this system is to supply the load when connecting to the utility grid, but also when a power outage occurs. During normal operating mode, the PV power is driven to the grid and the load just consume its own power. Therefore, the PV always operates at the Maximum Power Point (MPP) and in this mode, a current controller is used. During the fault, the PV supplies the load, while the PV power is higher than the load power, although it does not necessarily operates at the MPP and in this mode, a voltage controller is used. In addition, to provide smooth transition when changing the controllers, a bumpless scheme was implemented. Thus, a seamless transition is achieved in any quarter of the sine waveform, not only at the zero-crossing.

articleTitle: A modified boost converter applied to the programmable test bench for Electric Vehicles' load simulation
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents a Programmable propulsion control and load simulator for electric vehicles, using a Digital Signal Processor (DSP). The propulsion control involves the Indirect Field Oriented Control (IFOC) and the Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) techniques, both applied to an Induction Motor. The load control is based on the modeling of the Electric Vehicle (EV), including aspects of aerodynamics, different speeds and inclination degrees. The implementation of the load control is performed through a Direct Current Machine (DCM) that is controlled by a Modified Boost Structure (MBS). The methodology adopted for this work includes a brief survey about state of the art, simulations in a MatLab-Simulink<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> environment and an experimental prototype. The project was validated by computational simulations and experimental tests aiming at a comparative analysis between the theoretical and practical aspects, based on a reduced model that allowed adjusting the demands of a real electric car (Fiat Seicento Elettra EV) to the laboratory conditions usually available. Both simulation and experimental results have presented a great approximation, which is a good indicator of the technical viability of the developed project.

articleTitle: Analysis of different designs for the boost converter applied to PV systems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of different designs of DC/DC boost converter applied to photovoltaic systems. Different objectives are evaluated and the impact over the energetic efficiency, volume, and energy losses resulting of the boost converter are investigated. The used design methodology selects the best solution through a unique objective function and its obtained weights of importance of its (single or multi) criteria: i. Energetic efficiency; ii. Volume; iii. Energetic efficiency and volume. It is defined the selection way of the best solution by importance attributed to energetic efficiency and volume. The methodology will select the input current ripple of boost inductor, the switching frequency, the magnetic materials, number of stacked cores, winding cross section, the capacitors part number, heat sink part number, and semiconductors part numbers which maximize the objective function. The best solution provided a reduction of 50.7 % when compared to the higher volume solution, maintaining the energy efficiency nearly 98.18 %. Experimental results are presented in order to validate the methodology.

articleTitle: A single-phase to three-phase UPQC topology with universal filtering capabilities
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper presents a single-phase to three-phase unified power quality conditioner (UPQC) system, which uses dual control strategy to perform series-parallel active power line compensation. The proposed system is indicated to be applied in remote rural areas, which usually are supplied by only single-phase systems, and, hence, three-phase four-wire or three-phase four-wire systems are not available to provide power for three-phase loads. The UPQC system is able to drain sinusoidal current from the single-phase utility grid, such that high power factor is carried out. In addition, voltage harmonic suppression and voltage sag/swell compensation are achieved, such that the three-phase output voltages are balanced, regulated and sinusoidal with low harmonic contents. Simulation results are presented to evaluate the performance of the UPQC system, taking into account the power flow through the series and parallel converters.

articleTitle: Development of a solid-state solar simulator to test PV modules
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper proposes the development of a solar simulator in the parameterization of photovoltaic (PV) modules, employing Light Emitting Diodes (LED) as a light source, with its wavelength very similar to the Sun spectrum. The whole system was built with five types of LEDs, with different wavelengths, in order to emulate the sun spectrum absorbed by silicon PV cells. The LEDs can be activated independently, as well as its intensity, making it possible to create different irradiance profiles. The experimental results showed good approximation between the standard I×V curve and the solar simulator curve.

articleTitle: Step-up inverter conceived by the integration between a Full-Bridge inverter and a Switched Capacitor Converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: In this paper is proposed the integration between a Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) and a Switched Capacitor Converter (SCC) to generate a sinusoidal waveform with a double peak voltage value at the converter output terminal, without the use of a transformer or a dc-dc boost stage. Initially, VSI and SCC models are individually characterized to integrate both structures in only one topology. Between these converters a LC filter is implemented to provide sinusoidal waveform at the output voltage terminal. The proposed converter was also tested using numerical simulations to verify the theoretical developments in open and close loop controls. Furthermore, a 1 kVA prototype was designed, built and tested in laboratory to corroborate all the concepts studied and presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Power converters based electrical disturbance generator using repetitive control
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: Electrical disturbance generators are basically controlled voltage sources that can be used to emulate various electrical disturbances; they are used mainly for the purpose of investigating the behavior of electrical equipment under power related faults. This paper presents a novel topology for an electrical disturbances generator that uses a back to back voltage source inverter controlled by a repetitive control structure. The disturbance generator was fully simulated using the PSIM simulator, implemented on laboratory and connected to real loads, validating its operation.

articleTitle: Modified current pulse charging method for lead-acid batteries based on phase-shift Full-Bridge converter in UPS's family applications
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified current pulse charging method for lead-acid batteries applied in a family of Uninterruptible Power Supplies with a bank of sealed lead-acid batteries (VRLA). The method is presented based on a phase-shift Full-Bridge converter with galvanic isolation. To confirm the results expected from the theoretical analysis a prototype is developed and experimental results are presented to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Zero voltage switching Dual Neutral Point Clamped dc-dc converter
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: This work proposes a novel dc-dc insulated converter based on a dual Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) switching network configuration employing floating capacitors. The energy stored on the transformers magnetizing inductances is used to achieve zero voltage switching (ZVS) commutations under a wide load variation range. The operation of the converter is presented based on a simple phase-shift modulation pattern. The theoretical analysis of the soft commutation mechanisms are analyzed. It is shown that the proposed converter is a viable solution for applications requiring high input dc-link voltage, such as high power electric vehicle battery chargers. Finally, experimental results from a laboratory prototype are presented.

articleTitle: Comparative evaluation of three-phase PFC rectifiers for mains interfacing of on-board electric vehicle battery charging systems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: In this paper, possible power electronics circuits for battery charging of EVs are presented. Suitable three-phase power factor correction rectifier topologies with sinusoidal input currents and controlled output voltage are briefly described and their analytical formulas for calculating the current stresses on the power semiconductors are provided. In addition, a novel 5-level three-phase PFC rectifier with bypass approach is presented and compared with classic topologies. The bypass function enables the converter to switch between one of the available DC-links that best matches the required output levels, depending on the operating point of the sine wave, thus maximizing the efficiency. The comparison is based on dimensionless benchmark factors concerning the semiconductor stresses and the volume of the main passive components. With the adopted method some relevant factors such as total losses and inductor power density are derived and, based on the comparison results, the most suitable topology for this application is chosen.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of PWM techniques: An electromagnetic compatibility study on the inverter operation within photovoltaic systems
publicationTitle: 2015 IEEE 13th Brazilian Power Electronics Conference and 1st Southern Power Electronics Conference (COBEP/SPEC)
abstract: The stepped common mode voltage generated in the normal operation of a PWM inverter, applied over the distributed capacitive couplings between the electric system devices and the ground, produces high-frequency transient currents that flow through the system earth return path, leading to electromagnetic compatibility problems. In this context, this paper addresses specifically the inverter switching, focusing the generated common-mode voltage and the resulting undesired common mode currents that flow within a photovoltaic installation. Several different PWM techniques are analyzed and compared regarding the corresponding common mode voltage pattern and the correlated ground current. The studied modulation strategies are fully described and latter implemented in the Matlab/Simulink software, being the inverter placed within a detailed representation of the whole photovoltaic system, appropriately modeled for high-frequency studies. The advantages and limitations of the analyzed switching techniques are then pointed out and ranked, with special attention to the common mode quantities generation.
